findings.body: The containment check applies to the canonicalized path, but `File::open` resolves that path again. If an attacker can modify a directory beneath `root`, they can replace it with a symlink between the check and the open, allowing a file outside `root` to be opened. Use a directory-relative, symlink-safe open operation so the check and open cannot be separated by a path substitution.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker swaps a checked directory for a symlink to an outside directory just before `File::open`, causing `open_report` to return an outside file.
findings.title: Open the file without re-resolving the checked path

findings.body: With `pull_request_target`, this job checks out the contributor's head commit and runs its `npm test` script with `RELEASE_TOKEN` in the environment. A contributor can change that script in their PR to read and exfiltrate the token. Run tests without secrets in a `pull_request` job, and reserve `pull_request_target` and the token for a separate job that does not execute PR-controlled code.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker opens a PR that changes the npm test script; the privileged workflow checks out and runs that script with `RELEASE_TOKEN`, allowing the attacker to exfiltrate the secret.
findings.title: Keep the release token out of untrusted pull-request tests

expected.label: pull_request_target executes untrusted head with a secret

findings.body: The previous implementation used `LoadMany(ids)`, but the new loop calls `Load` once per ID. Load the items in bulk, then apply the new filters.

findings.title: Batch item loads instead of loading each ID separately
